text_blocks.snippet: Olmesartan, a medication for high blood pressure, was discontinued for some patients due to its association with a severe gastrointestinal condition called olmesartan-associated enteropathy (OAE). This condition, also known as sprue-like enteropathy, can cause symptoms like chronic, severe diarrhea, significant weight loss, and intestinal damage.
snippet_highlighted_words: due to its association with a severe gastrointestinal condition called olmesartan-associated enteropathy (OAE)

list.title: OAE Symptoms:
list.snippet: Patients taking olmesartan may experience chronic, non-bloody diarrhea, weight loss, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and bloating.

list.title: Diagnostic Challenges:
list.snippet: The symptoms of OAE can mimic other conditions like celiac disease, making diagnosis difficult. Symptoms can also appear months or even years after starting olmesartan, delaying diagnosis.

list.title: Intestinal Damage:
list.snippet: Biopsies of the small intestine may show villous atrophy and inflammation, similar to celiac disease.

list.title: Treatment and Resolution:
list.snippet: Discontinuing olmesartan and switching to another antihypertensive medication often leads to symptom resolution and intestinal healing. In some cases, steroids may also be used to manage inflammation.

list.title: FDA Action:
list.snippet: The FDA issued a warning about the link between olmesartan and sprue-like enteropathy, requiring label changes to include information about the potential for severe gastrointestinal side effects.

list.title: Public Citizen Petition:
list.snippet: Public Citizen filed a petition with the FDA to ban olmesartan-containing medications due to the risks of OAE.
